findings.world_state_read: The protagonist's parent/seat, visible seat entities, containing areas, parent chains, axis values, and placement/holding state.
findings.reason: The interaction and narration require the package's use_seated/take_text fields and the uses_thing callback, so the whole function stays in storygame. The world-only setup at lines 46-63 identifies the current seat and visible seats in the protagonist's area; lines 90-97 compare parent chains to prefer seats near the item or protagonist, while lines 98-100 apply the seat's enter axis.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.seating_state(self, entity_id: str) -> tuple[str | None, tuple[str, ...]] — return the entity's current declared seat and the visible declared seats in its containing area, preserving the existing sorted order and seat_for relationships.
findings.risks: Preserve sorted seat order, None when the protagonist has no seat or area, hidden-seat filtering, nested-area matching, enter_pole axis behavior, and the distinction between a seat's declared seat_for and the item being used. Do not move use_seated, take_text, enter_text, right_text, or callback/model decisions.

findings.world_state_read: Vehicle and seat kinds, visibility, parent/area context, containment chains, holder state, and movement into a seat.
findings.reason: Lines 135-146 build visible vehicle/visible-seat options from world entity IDs, which is world-only candidate discovery; lines 185-191 select candidates sharing the protagonist's area. The question callbacks, command matching, package enter/notice text, and returned command are storygame behavior and must remain there.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.visible_vehicle_seats(self, vehicle_ids: Iterable[str]) -> tuple[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]], ...] — return visible vehicle IDs with their visible declared seat IDs, in the current deterministic ordering.
findings.risks: World.seats already supplies visible seats for one entity; the proposed helper must not diverge from it. Preserve sorted vehicle/seat ordering, hidden seats and vehicles, same-area versus nested-area semantics, already-aboard exclusion, companion movement performed by World.move, and the current first-seat choice.

findings.world_state_read: The protagonist's seat and seat_for entity, all entity IDs, visibility, parent chains, holder relationships, area, and movement state.
findings.reason: The standing question and leave_text are story/prose behavior, but lines 244-252 construct a reachability set using only the seat relationship, visibility, chains, and holder relation. Line 259 is a client call to World.move; the moved helper should return IDs, leaving line 246's naming and the callback in storygame.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.reachable_from_seat(self, seat_id: str, protagonist_id: str) -> tuple[str, ...] — return visible entities on or under the seat's seat_for target, plus the seat and target themselves, preserving entity_ids order and held-by-protagonist entities.
findings.risks: Preserve the tuple order from World.entity_ids, inclusion of seat and seat_for even when not visible, visibility of nested contents, holder inclusion, None/invalid seat handling, and World.move's area/companion/seat semantics.

findings.world_state_read: Protagonist area, item areas, visibility, vehicle kind, fixed flags, holder, parent, and movement state.
findings.reason: Lines 29 and 32-45 select candidate entities using only IDs, world placement/visibility/kind/holder state, and fixed metadata; the rest asks the story callback, moves the item, and builds prose. The package's item.fixed bit can be normalized into a plain fixed-ID set before calling the world helper.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.takeable_candidates(self, item_ids: Iterable[str], protagonist_id: str, fixed_ids: Collection[str] = ()) -> tuple[str, ...] — return visible, non-vehicle, non-fixed, unheld items placed in the protagonist's same area, in caller-compatible order.
findings.risks: Preserve candidate sorting done at line 50, None area handling, nested-area behavior through World.area, hidden/closed-container visibility, holder versus direct-parent distinctions, vehicle exclusion, fixed schema/package reconciliation, and World.move refusal/companion behavior.

findings.world_state_read: The entity's parent chain and whether an ancestor ID contains or equals the entity.
findings.reason: This entire helper is a world-only parent walk: lines 19-24 repeatedly call World.parent until matching the requested ancestor. It should be a World method so traversal and every other client use one cycle-safe containment rule.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.contains(self, entity_id: str, ancestor_id: str) -> bool — return true when ancestor_id is the entity itself or appears in its nearest-to-farthest parent chain, with the same cycle termination and None handling as World.chain.
findings.risks: The current loop includes entity_id itself but has no seen-set; preserve self-containment while adding World.chain-style cycle protection. Preserve None termination and area parent behavior, and do not confuse this with text matching helpers named _contains elsewhere.

findings.world_state_read: The protagonist's current parent and containment relation to package-declared connection origins.
findings.reason: Lines 55 and 59 are client reads used to filter StoryPackage connections, while lines 52-82 perform movement-verb and entity-name text matching against package vocabulary. The parent walk itself is isolated in _contains; this function remains inseparable from package connections and prose/input vocabulary.
findings.risks: Keep package connection ordering, ambiguous-route rejection, via IDs, aliases, and movement verb matching in storygame. If _contains changes, preserve the current-place self-match behavior.

findings.world_state_read: The protagonist's current parent and whether the current place is already under the requested destination or a connection origin.
findings.reason: Lines 90, 93, and 98 use World only as a client while the function resolves package connections and reads story access facts at lines 102-104. It needs StoryPackage connections and FactStore access state, so only the containment helper should move.
findings.risks: Preserve no_route versus already_there precedence, package route order, access_closed fallback, and the fact predicate/value convention.

findings.world_state_read: An area's parent ancestors and all descendant areas in the area tree.
findings.reason: Lines 348-363 directly rebuild an area-tree index, walk parents, and repeatedly scan descendants. This is world topology, not narration safety; the helper should receive a World and an area ID, while the surrounding scene/nameability policy stays in storygame.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.related_area_ids(self, area_id: str) -> frozenset[str] — return the area itself, every area ancestor, and every area descendant using World.parent/World.entity_ids without depending on StoryPackage classes.
findings.risks: Preserve set semantics, the inclusion of the starting area, immutable schema area parents, descendant closure, malformed/missing parent handling, and cycle termination. World.chain covers the ancestor half but not descendants; do not replace the whole helper with chain alone.

findings.world_state_read: The nearest-to-farthest parent IDs of a location.
findings.reason: Lines 370-375 duplicate a parent-chain walk over location records. That is exactly world topology and can use the existing World.chain result after the narration validator obtains the adapter's World; the text/knowledge policy in _validate_segments remains in storygame.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.chain(self, entity_id: str) -> tuple[str, ...] (existing method; replace this helper with a call through the adapter-provided World).
findings.risks: Preserve current ancestor ordering and exclusion of the location itself. World.chain also handles fact-backed parents and cycle termination; ensure the adapter uses the same facts/schema represented by the current package records before switching callers.

findings.world_state_read: Protagonist area, fixed status, visibility, area kind, item area, and optional scope membership.
findings.reason: Lines 46-64 select fixed visible entities in the protagonist's area; that predicate can be a World helper if item IDs, fixed IDs, and an optional plain scope-ID set are supplied. Lines 70-88 perform command/name matching, the relocates_thing question, and fixed refusal prose, so the whole function must not move.
findings.proposed_world_method: World.fixed_visible_candidates(self, item_ids: Iterable[str], protagonist_id: str, fixed_ids: Collection[str] = (), scope_ids: Collection[str] | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...] — return fixed, visible, non-area items in the protagonist's area and optional supplied scope.
findings.risks: Preserve the in_scope override by converting it to a plain scope-ID set, schema/package fixed reconciliation, sorted candidate order, None-area behavior, visibility through closed containers, area exclusion, and the distinction between refusing a move and actually calling World.move.

findings.world_state_read: StoryPackage world schema data and the FactStore backend used to construct a World.
findings.reason: This is the intended storygame adapter: it translates package schema data and the story FactStore into a story-agnostic World instance. It does not implement world rules or walk the tree, and callers need the package-specific schema source.
findings.risks: Keep WorldSchema validation, FactStore fact construction, and the package-to-schema translation in the adapter. worldkeeper must not import StoryPackage or learn story IDs/vocabulary.

findings.world_state_read: Character kind and canonical entity name, plus package NPC unnamed-label and fact-gated naming state.
findings.reason: Line 44 uses World.is_a and line 48 uses World.name as client calls, but lines 45-47 apply StoryPackage NPC labels gated by story facts. The available display label is a story-facing concern, not a World method.
findings.risks: Preserve unnamed_label/named_by gating, unknown-ID naming behavior, and the distinction between canonical world names and player-available story labels.

findings.world_state_read: Pending story fact effects, world effect payloads, World.apply_effects results, and effect-application marker facts.
findings.reason: The function is an adapter/orchestrator: lines 76-80 select package-declared effects and translate them, line 81 delegates world mutation to the existing World.apply_effects method, and lines 82-86 record story refusals and markers. It needs StoryPackage effects, FactStore markers, and logging.
findings.risks: Preserve pending-effect ordering, one marker per fact, refusal logging, partial application behavior, and the effect mapping in _effect_dict. Do not move story fact IDs or WorldEffect vocabulary into worldkeeper.

findings.world_state_read: Scene placement parents, placement text, under/part_of relations, companions, parent IDs, and World.place/set_companion/clear_companion results.
findings.reason: Lines 92-130 interpret StoryPackage scene metadata and construct story-specific refusal records while delegating placement to World.place. Lines 131-150 coordinate package companions and use World parent/companion methods as clients; there is no local tree walk or duplicate placement rule to move.
findings.risks: Preserve group-before-character ordering, ItemPlacement type/None checks, text/under/part_of forwarding, companion clear/place/set ordering, refusal parent IDs, and World.place's hidden/fixed/setup semantics.

summary: The clearest boundary violations are the parent-tree walks in traversal and narration safety; the traversal walk duplicates World.chain behavior and the narration helpers duplicate ancestor logic while also rebuilding descendants. Seating, taking, and fixed-refusal functions mix story callbacks and prose with extractable world-only candidate or reachability predicates, while their orchestration remains in storygame. world_model.py is correctly an adapter/client layer: it constructs World, applies package effects and scene metadata, and formats story-facing names without reimplementing tree rules. Movers must preserve deterministic ordering, None handling, visibility through containers, area nesting, fixed flags, seat/companion behavior, and setup relations such as under and part_of.
